sectionHints.search_keywords: Each group is OR-merged into one query, then run once per city.
sectionHints.channels_http: Default timeout, retries and exponential backoff of channel requests.
sectionHints.channels_cascade: The main search uses only the first channel that is available (enabled, within budget, circuit closed) each cycle.
sectionHints.channels_jobspy: The python-jobspy service shared by linkedin-guest, indeed and jobspy-google. The proxy list may carry credentials, so it is not shown here: edit sources.yaml directly.
sectionHints.ai_order: The first one is tried first; on failure (quota used up, cooling down, offline) the next one takes over. Nodes read “vendor · access”; the API layer expands into the order below.
sectionHints.ai_tasks: One row per task: leave it alone to follow the global order and each provider's default model, or give it its own order and pick a model for each node.
sectionHints.ai_scoring_german: When a posting requires more of the local language (the market's) than me.yaml says, these points come off the match score; an empty level costs nothing. Computed in code, not by the prompt.
sectionHints.schedule_backup: The runner takes a pg_dump on the cron below (in the time zone above) into data/backups/, with your config and profile (data/config, data/profile) next to it as a .config.tgz. To restore, run scripts/ops/restore.sh --latest (see the backup guide); it picks the newest backup and checks it first.
sectionHints.notify_telegram: Rarely changed: Bot API URL, long-poll timeout, back-off and retries.
sectionHints.ui_salary_axis: Shared by the salary axis of the job detail page and the mini axis in tables. Unit: thousand a year in the market's base currency; a stated range that does not fit is cut at the ends.
sectionHints.ui_freshness: The freshness bar shortens as the job ages; past the warning line it turns yellow with a hatch texture.
sectionHints.breakdown_auto: Only used when the mode is "Automatic".
sectionHints.ai_priority_weights: Priority = the sum of weight × component (0 to 1), minus the German gap. Only the order matters; the number is never shown as a score.
sectionHints.ai_priority_seniority: 0 to 1: how well the seniority read from the title suits you.
sectionHints.ai_priority_location: 0 to 1: how well the place matches where you want to be.
sectionHints.schedule_suggest: Once a week the AI looks at the jobs you marked. Only the switch, the time and the main limits are here; the rest only sizes the prompt and lives in Advanced.
sectionHints.language_ai: Language codes: en, zh, de, fr, pt-BR … Changing the AI language does not rewrite earlier results; they keep their language and are marked.
sectionHints.language_channels: Empty = the interface default above. pnpm run doctor and pnpm sources:list also take --lang.
sectionHints.ai_scoring_criteria: Your own criteria, one sentence each, in any language (at most 10 per list, 300 characters each). They are sent to the AI with every job (like your other preferences). The score stays one 0–100 number; a dealbreaker puts a job into the 0–29 band.
sectionHints.salary_lookup: Off by default. Each lookup sends the company name, job title, seniority, city and country (never your profile or the JD) to the AI provider, which searches the web. It costs tokens and, with the Anthropic API, a fee per search. Which AI it uses is set under task overrides on the "AI" tab (task "Salary lookup").
sectionHints.salary_benchmark: Rebuilt after every cycle from the postings of the window that state a salary you can compare (base currency, per year).
sectionHints.ai_limits_quota: Job Radar's own cap on how often it calls Claude Code and Codex. It counts only Job Radar's own calls and cannot see your account's real usage, so it can only step in late, never early. Your own requests (scoring a job, translating) are not held by the per-cycle cap. 0 turns a cap off.
sectionHints.ai_scoring_evidence: Off by default: each score then also writes a short JD quote per reason, so the output tokens of the "score" task grow (compare its median on /ai-usage). Turning it on or off re-scores nothing.

telegram.intro:
Job Radar sends good matches and alerts through a Telegram bot of your own. This takes about two minutes:
  1. In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot and answer its two questions. It replies with a token like 123456789:AAE...
  2. Paste that token here (nothing is shown while you paste).
  3. Send any message to your new bot, so this command learns the chat id.
  4. A test message arrives; then the values go into .env and the services restart.

search_jobs.title: Search jobs
search_jobs.description: Search the jobs Job Radar collected: by keyword, city, work mode, minimum rank, minimum yearly salary, first-seen date and application status. Returns ranked job cards (facts, links, score and rank) without the JD text; use get_job for one job's details. Jobs the hard filter removed and closed jobs are left out. For "what is new today", pass since = today and sort = rank.

get_job.title: Get one job
get_job.description: One job in detail: facts, source links, score and rank, compensation and benefit signals with their JD quotes and positions, the number of AI traps found, your application's status, and the JD text after Job Radar removed text aimed at AI. When the trap check has not run for the job, the JD is withheld.

list_applications.title: List applications
list_applications.description: Your applications: status, when the status last changed, days in that status, next step and its date, interview rounds, the status history. Filter by status; stale_only lists only the applications waiting longer than the reminder thresholds (interested for more than N days without applying, applied for more than M days without an answer).

params.query: Free text: matches title, company, location and the JD
params.city: A city name, e.g. as the jobs list's city filter offers it
params.minRank: Lowest rank value (0-100) to keep; unscored jobs drop out
params.minAnnualSalary: Lowest stated yearly salary in the market's base currency; jobs without a stated salary drop out
params.since: First seen on or after this day (YYYY-MM-DD, in the Job Radar time zone)
params.until: First seen on or before this day (YYYY-MM-DD)
params.applicationStatus: Application statuses to keep (new also matches jobs without an application; archived = ignored)
params.sort: Order: rank (best first, default), posted (newest posting first), first_seen (newest found first)
params.limit: Most results to return (capped by mcp.yaml limits.max_results)
params.jobId: The job id (from search_jobs or list_applications)
params.staleOnly: Only applications waiting longer than the reminder thresholds

dealBreakers.title: Deal-breakers
dealBreakers.description: Rules that veto a job before any AI call. A vetoed job is not deleted: it shows under "Show filtered" with the rule's name, and "Keep anyway" on its page brings it back.
dealBreakers.aiNote: A condition you cannot write as a rule belongs in <criteria>Settings → AI → scoring criteria</criteria> under "unacceptable": the AI judges it, which still costs one scoring call.
dealBreakers.previewOnly: The counts are a preview over the jobs in the database now; saving applies the rules on the next filter run, and old scores stay valid.

fields.label: Name
fields.idHint: Recorded with each vetoed job; lower case, digits, - and _.
fields.termsHint: Whole words; case and accents are ignored ("Rust" does not match "trust").
fields.patternsHint: Regular expressions, case ignored. A repeated group must not repeat inside, like (a+)+.
fields.unlessHint: Regular expressions: a hit in a sentence that matches one of these does not count ("no travel").
